## Key steps in the shipping process


There are three essential stages in the ecommerce shipping process: receiving, processing, and fulfillment. Each step is critical to ensuring that the right product reaches the right customer on time.


### Order receiving


This is where it all starts. Your ecommerce platform captures the customer’s order, and your back-end systems must be ready to act—fast.


Modern ecommerce businesses operate across multiple channels: branded websites, online marketplaces like Amazon and Walmart, and even social commerce platforms. That’s why omnichannel fulfillment tools and ecommerce automation are essential.


By syncing incoming orders in real-time, you reduce the risk of overselling or delays. A centralized order dashboard helps you monitor order flow and ensure all customer data is accurate before fulfillment begins.


### Order processing


Once an order is received, your system verifies payment, checks stock availability, and routes the order to the right fulfillment center.


- **Order management systems (OMS)** automate these checks and help prioritize fulfillment based on shipping method or customer tier.
- **Inventory syncing prevents** “phantom inventory” issues—where an item appears in stock but isn’t.
- **Automation** here can trigger warehouse tasks, update customers with confirmation emails, and flag exceptions before they cause problems.


Tip: The faster you process, the sooner your team can fulfill—and the happier your customer will be.


### Order fulfillment & shipping


Order fulfillment includes multiple micro-steps, from product retrieval to final handoff. Let’s break it down:


#### Picking & packing


The **picking** process involves selecting the correct items from your warehouse inventory. There are several methods:


- **Batch picking** : Grouping similar orders to minimize walking time.
- **Zone picking** : Dividing the warehouse into zones for greater efficiency.
- **Wave picking** : Scheduling picking runs based on carrier pickup times.


Once picked, products are packed securely and branded where possible. Smart packaging decisions (like using the smallest possible box) can reduce shipping costs and minimize waste.


#### Labeling & documentation


Every shipment needs accurate shipping labels, barcodes, and—if it’s going international—customs documentation. These documents ensure that your package can be tracked and delivered efficiently.


Using automated label printing reduces human error and speeds up your workflow. Bonus: labels can be branded with your company logo or colors for a more polished look.


#### Carrier selection & shipping


Choosing the right shipping carriers is a balancing act between speed, cost, and reliability. Many ecommerce businesses now use multi-carrier shipping software to:


- Compare real-time rates
- Access discounted shipping rates
- Assign the best carrier based on location and urgency


Whether you're shipping with FedEx, USPS, UPS, DHL, or a regional courier, automating this decision can significantly lower costs and reduce delivery times.


#### Order tracking & delivery


Customers expect to know where their order is at every step. Real-time order tracking, automated shipping updates, and branded tracking pages improve transparency and reduce WISMO ("Where Is My Order?") calls to support.


When tracking is personalized and proactively delivered, your brand comes across as more professional—and more trustworthy.


#### Returns & reverse logistics


Returns aren’t just a post-purchase pain point—they’re a make-or-break moment for your customer experience. Shoppers expect a frictionless, hassle-free return process, and your ability to deliver can directly impact loyalty.


Here’s how top ecommerce brands manage their returns:


- **Easy-to-find return policies** : Make sure your return window, eligible items, and conditions are clearly stated on product and checkout pages.
- **Automated return labels** : Customers should be able to generate or receive a return label with minimal effort. Platforms like PitneyShip help automate this process based on rules you define.
- **Self-service portals** : Let customers initiate returns, select reasons, and view refund status online—reducing pressure on your support team.


But beyond convenience, there’s cost and sustainability to think about. Reverse logistics can get expensive quickly. That's why many brands are now:


- **Reselling returned goods** through secondary marketplaces
- **Refurbishing items** to reduce waste
- **Repackaging returned stock** for flash sales or outlet stores
- **Donating non-sellable returns** to meet CSR goals


**Real example** : A home goods retailer found that over 40% of returns were for minor packaging damage. By adding a “return reason” flow with photo uploads and offering a 20% refund without return, they saved thousands on return shipping and boosted CSAT scores.


## Parties involved in the shipping process


Shipping success depends on collaboration. Here are the key players:


### Shippers (retailers & sellers)


Shippers manage:


- **Carrier selection**
- **Order processing**
- **Customer communication** (like tracking emails or return instructions)


A reliable shipper ensures packaging is secure, policies are clear, and expectations are managed.


### Carriers (shipping providers)


Carriers are responsible for physically transporting packages. They impact:


- Delivery speed
- Last-mile experience
- Shipping rates


Businesses benefit from **rate negotiation** , **multi-carrier partnerships** , and **discounted options** through fulfillment software.


### Fulfillment centers & warehouses


Whether in-house or outsourced, fulfillment centers store inventory and handle picking and packing. Efficient warehouse management means fewer delays and happier customers.


### Third-party logistics (3PLs)


3PLs manage warehousing, shipping, and returns on behalf of ecommerce brands. They’re ideal for growing businesses that want to scale fast and reduce overhead. Many 3PLs also offer negotiated carrier rates and value-added services like kitting or international compliance.


### Customers


Customers shape your shipping strategy. They expect:


- Fast, affordable delivery options
- Clear tracking
- Easy returns


Meeting these expectations drives loyalty, increases satisfaction, and boosts your brand’s reputation.


## Importance of ecommerce shipping processes


Shipping doesn’t just move products—it moves your brand reputation. A well-structured shipping process is the engine behind every positive review, repeat order, and customer referral.


Here’s why it matters:


- **Customer satisfaction** – 87% of shoppers say delivery experience directly impacts their decision to buy again. A delayed, damaged, or confusing delivery can ruin even the best product.
- **Cost control** – Shipping is one of the largest operational expenses in ecommerce. Optimizing packaging dimensions, negotiating carrier rates, and batching orders can drastically reduce overhead.
- **Scalability** – Without streamlined workflows, growing order volume can turn into chaos. Businesses with automation in place are better positioned to scale during peak seasons without adding headcount.
- **Brand differentiation** – Offering faster delivery, eco-friendly options, or branded packaging sets you apart from competitors.


Brands that treat shipping like a growth lever—not a cost center—see bigger returns in loyalty, retention, and margin.


## Shipping process best practices


If you want to optimize your ecommerce shipping process, these best practices aren’t just tips—they’re operational pillars that keep your fulfillment running smoothly, even as your business scales.


- **Use shipping automation** – Automating key tasks like label printing, carrier assignment, and shipping notifications saves hours of manual work. It also ensures consistency—especially during peak times when errors are more likely. Look for shipping software that syncs directly with your ecommerce platform to eliminate gaps.
- **Offer multiple shipping options** – Today’s customers expect choice. Some prioritize speed, others want free shipping, and some will pay for same-day delivery. Providing options—like standard, expedited, and same-day—allows you to meet varied expectations and increase cart conversions.
- **Negotiate carrier rates** – Don’t settle for default rates. Use your shipping volume as leverage to negotiate better deals with multiple carriers.[Multi-carrier shipping software](https://www.pitneybowes.com/us/shipping-software.html) like PitneyShip can help you access discounted shipping rates and automate the selection of the most cost-effective carrier for each order.
- **Streamline returns management** – A messy return experience can turn customers away for good. Automate return label generation, offer QR-code drop-offs, and make refund tracking easy. Not only does this reduce support tickets, it increases customer satisfaction.
- **Integrate with ecommerce platforms** – Whether you’re on Shopify, WooCommerce, or BigCommerce, integrating your shipping software ensures real-time syncing of order data, inventory levels, and tracking. This eliminates manual errors, speeds up fulfillment, and provides customers with a seamless experience from cart to delivery.


**Pro tip** : Audit your shipping process quarterly. Look at fulfillment speed, delivery accuracy, cost per shipment, and return rates. Identify bottlenecks and test changes in a controlled way—small tweaks can yield big gains.
